title: Snoozer goes to New York with Whiteman and quits
summary: Snoozer arrives on New Year's Eve, is kept up entertaining Whiteman's friends, and writes that he is quitting.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: And so he told Snoozer, he said, you'll hear, you'll hear from me. And nobody paid any attention to it, you see. So Snoozer gave him my address at Karns, because Snoozer was going back to Bogalusa, you see. So Snoozer gave him my address at Karns and told him that if he wanted to get in touch with him, get in touch with him through me, you see. And I had Snoozer's address in Bogalusa. It's New Year's Eve night and we're playing, like I told you, the dinner where the blue room is. And that was a Venetian room then, I think. And we're up there and then the band's all knocked out. And strange as it may seem, Bill, in those days I didn't drink. But the whole band, New Year's Eve, Freddie Newman's men almost under the piano and everybody's loaded, you know, and nothing you could do about it. So I look at the entrance and here comes somebody who's got an overcoat on, he's got the collar up like this and it comes all the way down to his ankle, you see. And he's coming across the bandstand and he reaches in his pocket and he's got a pint of gin in each in each pocket like that. I say, oh, that's all I need, you know. A Snoozer. I had gotten a wire from Whiteman a few days before and I sent word to him over in Bogalusa, you see. And he was coming in to go to New York to join Whiteman. That's another thing I got that I had, I wish I had. I had to, it's the most pitiful letter you ever heard in your life, Bill. He wrote me, it must have been 10, 12 pages after he got to New York. And they never did put him in the band. All Whiteman used him first to take him around to these parties and entertain Whiteman's friends at these parties. The guy couldn't get any sleep at all, Bill.

Because guys like all the music, everybody that heard of him, the musicians, oh, they wouldn't go up to his hotel room, the poor guy could never sleep. But guys like Eddie Lang and all those guys, Dick McDonough was there, Carl Crest and all those guys were the big ones then. And then all the guys had the guy playing night and day and he was the kind of guy that couldn't say no, you know, never could say no to you. And did you ever see him?

Well, Snoozer was born, when he was born, they had to use forceps. And his head was lopsided like that from the forceps. His head came to almost a point, he was a funny looking guy. It was caused by the forceps when he was born. His head come, instead of coming out like that, his head went like that. See, almost into a point. And that overcoat that he had on. Like I tell you, he went and then this letter was telling me after he was up there about a month, month or that, that he was going to quit. That he just couldn't take it anymore. They wouldn't let him sleep and he wasn't making any records and anything like that. So he quit, why didn't he come on home. Never did go out of town anymore after that.
